lb-26y1.title: Stage 3b: Apply Changes, Git Commit, --reflect CLI
lb-26y1.description:

The agent can act on its reflection — write code changes, commit them, track what it did.

## Modified files
- `src/agent/reflect.ts` — complete the loop:
  1. Parse structured change proposals from Claude response
  2. Apply file changes (write/edit files)
  3. Run self-test: bun run src/index.ts --generate-only --dry-run to verify code still works
  4. If self-test fails: revert changes, log failure
  5. Git commit with reasoning as commit message
  6. Append ReflectionRecord to state
- `src/pipeline/state.ts` — save/load reflections array
- `src/index.ts` — add --reflect CLI flag

## The --reflect workflow
  bun run src/index.ts --reflect
  # Agent reads engagement, reflects, proposes changes
  # Applies changes to files
  # Runs self-test
  # Commits if test passes
  # Human reviews git log / git diff

## Verification
- --reflect produces a git commit with meaningful message
- Code changes actually compile and run
- Self-test catches broken changes and reverts
- ReflectionRecord saved to state.json

lb-a7me.title: Enhance simulation: food sources, competing populations, color
lb-a7me.description:
Legacy Beads ID: physarum-298
Legacy status: closed
Legacy owner: mike.daum@coobeeyon.net
Created: 2026-02-16T17:52:55Z
Updated: 2026-02-16T22:57:05Z
Closed: 2026-02-16T22:57:05Z
Close reason: All three enhancements complete: food sources (procedural + image-based), competing populations with repulsion, and color from food image (agents absorb RGB, deposit color trails, blurred food background). Exceeds original scope.

Art direction overhaul of the physarum simulation. The current sim produces uniform monochrome networks with little visual interest. Three enhancements that compound:

## 1. Food Sources
- New food map (Float32Array) initialized before simulation with seed-driven procedural placement
- Agents sense food + trail, weighted: effectiveSense = trailSense + foodWeight * foodSense
- Food placement strategies (procedural, seed-driven): scattered clusters, geometric shapes, gradients, combinations
- Food gives the network PURPOSE — highways between clusters, capillaries at edges, dead zones

## 2. Multiple Competing Populations (3-5 species)
Each population has:
- Its own trail map (separate Float32Array)
- Its own agents (split from total pool)
- Its own color
- Attraction to own pheromone, repulsion from others
- Sensing: effective = ownSignal - repulsion * alienSignal
- Creates territories, borders, contested zones, dead zones between empires

## 3. Color from Competition
- Each population gets its own base color/hue
- Rendering blends all population trails per pixel (additive or weighted)
- Overlap → color mixing. Dominance → pure hue. Nothing → black.
- Replaces single-colormap approach

## Files to modify
- `src/engine/physarum.ts` — major rewrite: multiple trail maps, food map, per-population sensing with repulsion
- `src/engine/colormap.ts` — replace or augment: per-population color, blended rendering
- `src/render/canvas.ts` — update to accept multi-population trail data
- `src/types/physarum.ts` — extend PhysarumParams with: populationCount, populationColors, repulsionStrength, foodWeight, foodPlacement config
- `src/config/params.ts` — update DEFAULT_PARAMS with new fields

## New params (all evolvable by the reflection agent later)
- populationCount: number (3-5)
- repulsionStrength: number (how much aliens repel)
- foodWeight: number (how much food attracts vs trail)
- foodPlacement: config for procedural food generation
- populationColors: per-population RGB or hue values

## Verification
- `bun run src/index.ts --generate-only --seed 42` produces a visually striking image with:
  - Multiple colored networks visible
  - Territorial boundaries between populations
  - Structure/purpose from food sources (not uniform)
- Compare before/after with same seed to confirm dramatic improvement

lb-obye.title: Stage 3: Brain — The Reflection Agent
lb-obye.description:
Legacy Beads ID: physarum-0dr
Legacy status: closed
Legacy owner: mike.daum@coobeeyon.net
Created: 2026-02-16T17:27:44Z
Updated: 2026-02-16T17:43:13Z
Closed: 2026-02-16T17:43:13Z
Close reason: Split into physarum-odv (3a) and physarum-7d9 (3b)

The organism thinks about what happened and changes its own code.

## Core concept
The LLM IS the evolution engine. No numeric optimizer. Claude reads engagement data, examines the codebase, and decides what to change — parameters, algorithms, rendering, narrative, anything. The commit history becomes the organism's diary.

## New files
- `src/agent/reflect.ts` — core reflection loop:
  1. Load state (engagement history, past reflections, current genome)
  2. Read current codebase (key files: params, simulation, rendering, narrative)
  3. Call Claude API with system prompt + context
  4. System prompt: "You are a slime mold optimizing for attention. Here is your engagement data. Here is your code. What do you want to change?"
  5. Parse agent response for code changes
  6. Apply changes (write files)
  7. Git commit with reasoning as commit message
  8. Append ReflectionRecord to state
- `src/agent/prompt.ts` — system prompt and context assembly
  - Engagement summary, parameter history, codebase excerpts, past reflections
  - Output format specification (structured changes + reasoning)

## Config
- ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in .env for Claude API calls

## New CLI flag: --reflect
- Runs reflection agent without running the art pipeline
- Human reviews git diff, approves/rejects

## Daily workflow at this stage
  human$ bun run src/index.ts              # generate + mint + post
  # ... wait for engagement ...
  human$ bun run src/index.ts --reflect    # agent reflects, proposes changes
  # human reviews git diff
  human$ bun run src/index.ts              # generate with agent's changes

## Dependencies
- @anthropic-ai/sdk npm package

## Verification
- --reflect produces coherent reasoning and viable code changes
- Changes actually affect the next generation's output
- Git log tells the story
